clue.text: Everyman in area set up for renovation with toolbox item

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it
renovating something means rebuilding it, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: the setter, Everyman, refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A house is being done up, and the setter is in the room with his toolbox.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's name stands for ME; it goes among the letters of AREA SET UP, and the whole lot is rearranged into TAPE MEASURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Any handyman's kit holds a retractable ruler for taking lengths, so the answer is an example of what a toolbox contains.

clue.text: Etonians managed without a worry

indicators.note: without means leaving something out, so one letter is dropped
managed letters have been handled and organised into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Pupils from Eton got by without any anxiety at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one A out of ETONIANS and rearrange the remaining seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is a state of mental strain and unease, a close synonym for a nagging concern.

clue.text: Noisily, dad cuts veg

indicators.note: noisily tells us the words are to be heard spoken rather than read

blocks.note: pa is dad, and snips means cuts

explanation.surface: Father is clattering about the kitchen chopping vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, PA SNIPS and PARSNIPS sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsnips are pale root vegetables, and veg is the everyday British short form for vegetables.

clue.text: 9am to rise and dress

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: An alarm goes at nine in the morning: time to get up and get dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: '9am' reads as a clock time, but the setter wants the numeral written the Roman way, followed by the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxi is a long garment reaching the ankles, short for maxi dress.

clue.text: Again, get in dubious cosmetic terminology

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, an example of such a term rather than a noun for it

indicators.note: something dubious is unreliable, so the letters cannot be trusted to stay in their order

explanation.surface: Another sceptical swipe at the doubtful jargon used to sell face creams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dubious' doubles as a sly comment on beauty-industry claims.
explanation.definitionFit: Creams and serums are marketed with a label promising to stop wrinkles, a term from the beauty industry's sales vocabulary.

clue.text: Clockwork Orange author's innermost desires

indicators.note: innermost keeps only the inside, so the outside letters at each end are lost

blocks.note: Anthony Burgess wrote A Clockwork Orange

explanation.surface: A literary query about the private longings of the novelist behind A Clockwork Orange.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the first and last letters from BURGESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Urges are strong wishes or impulses, so the plural noun matches the longings named in the clue.

clue.text: Primarily, entities numbering nine envisaged as discrete sets?

definitions.text: Primarily, entities numbering nine envisaged as discrete sets?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so each word gives only its opening letter

blocks.clueFragment: entities numbering nine envisaged as discrete sets
blocks.note: the initial letters of seven consecutive words

explanation.surface: A mathematical musing on how to think of groups of nine things.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: its initials spell the answer, and the words describe it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ennead is a group or set of nine, from the Greek for nine, so the plural names such sets.

clue.text: But ... but misprinted Bible hasn't one representation of idea

indicators.note: a misprint puts letters in the wrong places, so this word's letters are jumbled
something that hasn't a thing is lacking it, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: but and though both introduce a contrast
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone splutters about a faulty printing of the Bible missing a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word does two different jobs: the first is a synonym, THOUGH; the second is jumbled to TBU; then BIBLE loses its I.
explanation.definitionFit: In comics, a cloud-shaped balloon shows what a character is thinking, a drawn picture of a notion.

clue.text: Invite disaster when raft's rulebook thrown out

indicators.note: things thrown out are scattered in disorder, so the letters land in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Throwing away the safety manual on a raft is a recipe for catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to behave in a way that is likely to bring problems upon yourself, courting calamity.

clue.text: Chicken, headless bird reflected, finally complex psychedelic figure

indicators.note: without a head means the opening letter is chopped off
a reflection shows things back to front, so this word runs right to left
finally points to the very end, keeping only the closing letter

explanation.surface: A surreal sequence of poultry, a beheaded bird and a mirror, ending up in a 1960s haze.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRD loses its B, and the remaining IRD is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimi Hendrix was the guitarist whose acid-rock music defined the late-1960s hallucinogenic era.

clue.text: Silver fork's prongs grabbed hearty stews

indicators.note: to grab something is to hold it within, so one piece is clasped inside another

blocks.note: tines are the points of a fork
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A silver fork digs into a rich, warming casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagines are slow-cooked North African dishes of meat and vegetables, named after the clay pot used to make them.

clue.text: Remove tip from inflammation for wedding, perhaps

indicators.note: removing the tip means cutting off the first letter

blocks.note: a bunion is an inflamed swelling on the foot

explanation.surface: Advice to get a painful swelling sorted before walking down the aisle.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is one example of a joining together of two people, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Timeless, fat, ultimately fictional man!

indicators.note: timeless means without time, and time is T, so that letter is dropped
ultimately points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: An exclamation about an ageless, portly character who never really existed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: Shakespeare's knight is timeless, fat and fictional. 'Man' is the verb, as in to man a desk.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John is Shakespeare's celebrated stout, boastful knight in Henry IV and The Merry Wives of Windsor, an enduring comic creation.

clue.text: Friendly and well served with charming interior

indicators.note: an interior is what lies inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: in tennis, a player who has aced has served unreturnably

explanation.surface: A description of a tennis player who is personable, serves well and has a likeable inner nature.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are on familiar terms know each other socially, which is close to being on cordial terms.

clue.text: Applause given to guitar style considered best

blocks.note: to give someone a hand is to applaud them
picked guitar is played by plucking the strings individually

explanation.surface: A crowd cheers a guitarist whose playing technique is judged the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chosen with care, one at a time, is selected as the top choice from what is available.

clue.text: Person at computer rejected just over 57% of résumés

indicators.note: four sevenths is about 57.1 per cent, so only that share of the word's letters survives and the rest are cut
rejected suggests being sent back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A hiring manager at a screen throws out most of the CVs that arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: RESUMES has seven letters; four of them (RESU) are 57.14%, just over 57%, then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone operating a computer or software is called its user, the standard term in computing.

clue.text: Night out: wrap up with club

indicators.note: up can mean in turmoil, as in things being up in the air, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: An evening out ends with a visit to a nightclub, so wrap up warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour of several drinking establishments in one evening is a typical British way of spending an evening on the town.

clue.text: Clever pig (term of endearment)

blocks.note: first meaning: the sheep-herding piglet from the 1995 film
second meaning: an affectionate way to address a loved one

explanation.walkthrough: The bracket makes the second meaning look like an aside about calling someone a clever pig.
explanation.definitionFit: The film's porcine hero learns to herd sheep, and the same word is a fond name for a sweetheart.

clue.text: Geordie wearing suit for charity performance

indicators.note: something wearing clothes is inside them, so one piece is wrapped in another

blocks.note: to suit something is to befit it
a Geordie comes from Newcastle in north-east England, NE

explanation.surface: A Newcastle man puts on a suit for a fundraising show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like the clothing, but it is the verb meaning befit.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is a concert or show staged to raise money for a cause or person.

clue.text: Brownish water glass not holding litre

indicators.note: not holding something means it has been let go, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: a burn is a Scottish stream
a tumbler is a drinking glass
L is the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: A tumbler of brown-tinged water that is not quite full.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnt umber is a dark reddish-brown pigment, so the answer names a shade within the brown family.

clue.text: Oddly blue with pay rise and happy to get swindled

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd-numbered positions, first and third
in a down entry, rising means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: the first and third letters of blue
up means cheerful, as in feeling up

explanation.surface: Someone is strangely glum about a salary increase yet cheerful about being conned.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom, from selling a worthless young dog, means to be cheated into a bad purchase.

clue.text: Disraeli, noted Israelite

blocks.note: first meaning: the first name of the Victorian prime minister
second meaning: Jacob's youngest son, founder of one of the twelve tribes

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one description of Disraeli, who was of Jewish descent, but it holds two separate people.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the Victorian statesman and the youngest son of Jacob in Genesis share this given name.

clue.text: A little roadie unloads, getting cheers

indicators.note: a little of something is only a part of it, so the letters lie inside the words

explanation.surface: A crew member unpacks the gear after the gig and gets thanked.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is informal British for goodbye, and the French farewell means the same parting word.

clue.text: Reportedly, bashful bear that's hunted for fur

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the animal rather than a noun

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard from others, so the words are taken by their spoken sound

blocks.note: coy is bashful, and Pooh is A. A. Milne's bear

explanation.surface: A shy bear is said to be pursued for its pelt.
explanation.walkthrough: The bear in the surface is a red herring for the animal itself: a coypu is a large South American rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu, or nutria, is a beaver-like rodent farmed and trapped for its pelt.

clue.text: Ras Tafari, somewhat elevated emperor

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the words, so the letters are found inside them
in a down entry, elevated means lifted so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: the opening letters of these words

explanation.surface: Ras Tafari became Emperor Haile Selassie of Ethiopia, raised to the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was a Russian emperor, the title derived from Caesar.

clue.text: The French newspaper is essentially ultra Marxian

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letter is taken

explanation.surface: A French paper is described as fundamentally far left.
explanation.definitionFit: A Marxian thinker holds socialist views on the political left, so the noun can stand as a left-wing adherent.

clue.text: Area of skin peeled, removing outer layers – using this?

definitions.text: Area of skin peeled, removing outer layers – using this?

indicators.note: taking off outer layers strips letters from both ends, two from each side

blocks.note: the scalp is the skin of the head

explanation.surface: A surgeon peels back skin, and the question is what tool would do it.
explanation.walkthrough: PEELED loses PE and ED from its ends, leaving EL; the whole clue describes what the answer is used for.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's small, very sharp blade is the instrument that would cut away layers of skin.

clue.text: Chandler put out by big surprise

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Raymond Chandler, or a candle-maker, is left upset by a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden sound of thunder is used figuratively for an astonishing, unexpected event, a bolt from the blue.
